name: Non-Immigrant O Visa (Retirement) and 1-Year Retirement Extension
summary: The standard route to retire in Thailand if you are 50 or older. You enter on a 90-day Non-Immigrant O visa, then turn it into a 1-year stay at a Thai immigration office by showing 800,000 THB in a Thai bank, 65,000 THB a month in income, or a mix of both. You renew the extension every year.
seoTitle: Thailand Retirement Visa (Non-O): 800,000 THB Rule and 1-Year Extension
seoDescription: How the Non-Immigrant O retirement visa works for over-50s: 800,000 THB or 65,000 THB a month, bank seasoning rules, the 1-year extension, fees and documents.
validity: The visa is valid for 3 months for a single entry and gives you up to 90 days in Thailand. After that, a retirement extension gives you up to 1 year at a time.
extendableDetail: Yes. Before your 90 days run out, apply at your local immigration office for a 1-year extension of stay based on retirement (form TM7, fee 1,900 THB). You can repeat this every year as long as you still meet the money rules.
feeNote: The visa fee is 2,000 THB on the Thai fee schedule for a single entry. Embassies charge it in local currency, so the exact amount depends on where you apply. Each 1-year extension in Thailand costs 1,900 THB.
financialRequirement: Choose one: at least 800,000 THB in a bank account, a monthly income or pension of at least 65,000 THB, or a combination of savings and yearly income that adds up to at least 800,000 THB. For the visa itself the money can be in a bank at home. For the 1-year extension it must be in a Thai bank account in your name, usually for 2 months before your first extension and 3 months before later ones, and you must keep at least 400,000 THB in the account between renewals.
processingTime: Processing times depend on the embassy. Some quote around 15 working days for the visa. An extension application is often decided the same day or within a few weeks, sometimes after an interim "under consideration" stamp.
keyRequirements: You are 50 or older on the day you apply.
You have 800,000 THB in savings, 65,000 THB a month in income, or a combination worth 800,000 THB a year.
Your passport is valid for at least 6 more months.
For the 1-year extension, the money sits in a Thai bank account in your own name for the required period.
You don't work in Thailand. Employment of any kind is not allowed on this visa.
documents: Passport valid for at least 6 months, with blank pages
Recent passport-style photo (taken within the last 6 months)
Bank statements for the last 3 months showing at least 800,000 THB, or proof of a monthly income of at least 65,000 THB
Proof of where you are now (for example a valid visa or residence permit in the country where you apply)
Flight booking and accommodation booking in Thailand
For the extension: form TM7, a 4x6 cm photo and copies of your passport pages
For the extension: a letter from your Thai bank confirming the balance, plus an updated bank book
For the extension: proof of your address in Thailand (a TM30 receipt, rental contract or house book)

howToApply.detail: Decide whether you will use savings, income or a combination. If you will use savings for the extension later, open a Thai bank account early so the money can "season" for the required months.

howToApply.step: Apply for the Non-O visa online
howToApply.detail: Apply on the official Thailand e-Visa site (thaievisa.go.th), choosing retirement as the purpose. Upload your passport, photo, proof of location and bank statements, then pay the fee.

howToApply.step: Enter Thailand and fill in the TDAC
howToApply.detail: Submit the free Thailand Digital Arrival Card in the 3 days before you arrive. You get up to 90 days on entry.
Keep 800,000 THB (or the right mix) in a Thai account in your name, or arrange proof of income that your immigration office will accept.
Before your 90 days end, take form TM7, your passport, photos, bank letter and bank book, proof of address and 1,900 THB to the immigration office that covers your address.

howToApply.step: Stay compliant and renew every year
howToApply.detail: Report your address every 90 days, get a re-entry permit before any trip abroad, keep at least 400,000 THB in the account and show 800,000 THB again before each renewal.

bestFor: Retirees aged 50+ who want to live in Thailand year-round
People who can show savings of 800,000 THB or a steady pension
Anyone who prefers to apply from home and sort out the long stay once in Thailand
notFor: People who want to work, including local jobs
Retirees married to a Thai citizen who would rather use the lower 400,000 THB marriage route
People who can't keep money in a Thai bank account
commonMistakes: Moving the 800,000 THB into Thailand too late, so it hasn't been in the account long enough before the extension
Leaving Thailand without a re-entry permit, which cancels your 1-year extension
Assuming every embassy still issues income letters for the 65,000 THB route

faqs.q: Do I need the money in a Thai bank to get the visa?
faqs.a: Not for the visa itself. The e-Visa asks for bank statements from any bank. For the 1-year extension in Thailand, the money must be in a Thai bank account in your name.

faqs.q: How long must the 800,000 THB stay in the account?
faqs.a: The common rule is 2 months before your first extension and 3 months before later ones. After approval you usually keep the full amount for 3 months, then never let it drop below 400,000 THB. Offices differ, so ask yours.

faqs.q: Can I combine savings and pension?
faqs.a: Yes. A mix of money in the bank and yearly income that adds up to at least 800,000 THB is accepted.
Not for this route. Mandatory health insurance applies to the Non-Immigrant O-A long-stay visa, which you apply for from abroad. Insurance is still a very good idea.

faqs.q: Can my spouse come with me?
faqs.a: Usually yes. A spouse under 50 can normally get a Non-O visa as your dependant, with your marriage certificate. Check the exact rules with the embassy and your immigration office.

faqs.q: Can I work on a retirement extension?
faqs.a: No. Employment of any kind is not allowed on a retirement visa or extension.

faqs.q: What happens if I leave Thailand?
faqs.a: Get a re-entry permit first (1,000 THB single, 3,800 THB multiple). Without one, your extension ends when you leave.
